description: Example template task file showing the standardized task structure based on phase9-tasks.json
usage: Copy this template to create new tasks. Adjust fields as needed for your specific task.

metadata.author: Kiro AI Agent
metadata.purpose: Template for creating new tasks in the phase task system

exampleTask.name: Documentation Inventory and Content Review
exampleTask.modelRationale: File inventory, classification, metadata extraction. DeepSeek V4-Flash is 70% cheaper than Haiku with comparable quality for file ops.
deliverables: Inventory documentation across the repository, including Markdown, text, and API reference files
Read each document's metadata and actual contents before deciding its destination or disposition
Classify documents as active, completed, historical, duplicate, or obsolete
Identify canonical topic documents, conflicting guidance, inbound links, and ownership

exampleTaskWithDependencies.name: Redundant Documentation Consolidation
exampleTaskWithDependencies.modelRationale: Complex comparison and conflict resolution. GPT-4o mini offers 7.5/10 reasoning at fraction of cost. Escalate to GPT-4.1 or R1 if reasoning insufficient.
deliverables: Compare metadata summaries and actual text to detect duplicate or overlapping material
Merge redundant documentation into one canonical file per topic and reconcile conflicting guidance
Preserve unique, current information and maintain distinct documents where audiences or interfaces differ
Update inbound references before removing superseded duplicate files

examplePipelineTask.name: Pipeline Catalog and Execution Ledger
examplePipelineTask.modelRationale: CRITICAL: Schema design, event store architecture. GPT-4o mini surprisingly capable. Escalate to GPT-4.1 for foundational design.
deliverables: Define a registry of named pipelines with stable pipeline IDs, versions, stages, inputs, outputs, and verification checks
Persist every pipeline run with run ID, task ID, workspace, timestamps, status, stage results, errors, and cancellation state
Record model, provider, token, cost, documentation sources, tool calls, changed files, and validation results when applicable
Store execution records in a workspace-scoped append-only JSONL or SQLite event store with retention and redaction controls
Expose querying and export for a task, pipeline, session, date range, or failed stage
Add tests proving incomplete or failed pipeline runs cannot be reported as completed

exampleSecurityTask.name: Execution Permissions and Workspace Safety
exampleSecurityTask.modelRationale: CRITICAL: Security boundaries, path validation, secret redaction. o1-mini for reasoning. Escalate to Opus for maximum safety.
deliverables: Provide clear approval modes for read-only, approval-required, and explicitly trusted operations, with safe defaults
Require confirmation for terminal commands and file writes according to policy and show the exact command, working directory, or target files
Constrain file operations to the selected workspace and guard against traversal, symlink escapes, and destructive commands
Redact secrets from prompts, tool output, and logs, and require explicit consent before sending source to a cloud provider
Add security tests for path escapes, command policy, secret redaction, cancellation, and denied operations

exampleTaskWithCompletion.name: Shared Core and Interface Adapter Architecture
exampleTaskWithCompletion.modelRationale: CRITICAL: Architecture design. GPT-4o mini for most work. Escalate for complex architectural decisions.
deliverables: Define stable shared application services independent of any transport or user interface
Define interface adapter contracts for configuration, inputs, outputs, errors, and lifecycle
Create separate application access points that reuse the shared core without duplicating business logic
Propagate model-required and provider-unavailable outcomes consistently across interfaces
Add adapter-level contract tests and configuration isolation

pattern1_fileOperations.description: For simple file operations, implementations, and standard patterns

pattern2_moderateReasoning.description: For tasks requiring moderate reasoning but not security-critical

pattern3_securityCritical.description: For security-critical tasks requiring specialized reasoning
pattern3_securityCritical.note: Security should never be compromised for cost savings

pattern4_criticalArchitecture.description: For critical tasks requiring deep reasoning but not security-specific
pattern4_criticalArchitecture.note: Start with GPT-4o mini, escalate to o1-mini if reasoning insufficient

requiredFields.description: Array of recommended models in priority order (lowest cost first)

requiredFields.example: Explain why these models and when to escalate
requiredFields.description: Explanation of model selection and escalation triggers
Array of task IDs that must be completed first

optionalFields.description: Files or artifacts produced by this task
Description of what is blocking this task

priorityGuidelines.CRITICAL: Must complete; affects multiple other tasks; no alternatives
priorityGuidelines.HIGH: Important feature; significant value; some workarounds
priorityGuidelines.MEDIUM: Nice to have; adds value; can be deferred
priorityGuidelines.LOW: Enhancement; minor impact; can be skipped
